archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (possession-first)
archetype.definition: Detroit is out-shooting and out-chancing most of the league at 5-on-5, but the worst finishing in the NHL, a leaky penalty kill and an uneven goalie split have left it last in the Atlantic.

report.headline: The best Red Wings process in years, buried under the league's worst finishing
report.take:
For five straight seasons Detroit was an outshot team, with an xGF % between .459 and .488 every year. Its records were often propped up by close-game luck, including +5.4 in Pts vs Goal Diff last season. This year that has flipped. The Red Wings carry a .531 xGF % (8th) and a .52 CF % (9th). They put 28.8 shots a game on net (8th) and allow only 23.3 (5th), well under the league's 27. By how the ice tilts, this is a top-ten team. By the standings it is 7-8-3, last in the division, 22nd on the site.

The gap is almost entirely about the puck going in. Detroit's skaters are shooting .091 in all situations, dead last in the league against a league average of .116. That is why a team generating chances ranks 27th in offense at 2.72 goals a game. The other side has its own leak. The all-situations save % is .886 (20th) and the penalty kill is 69%, 28th and well under the league's .77. Put together, the all-situations PDO of 97.6 ranks 30th. Teams that low rarely stay there.

The goaltending is really two stories. Daniil Tarasov has a .919 save % and +6.5 GSAx in six starts, 11th on the goalie tab. John Gibson has a .860 and -5.9 GSAx across 11 starts, 57th of 69. The team GSAx of +1.6 looks average only because the two cancel out. That D+ grade is a usage choice as much as a talent problem. Up front the scoring is thin. Raymond, DeBrincat and Arvidsson have 15-16 points each, and Emmitt Finnie (7 goals, +9) has been a real find. Copp and Rasmussen are playing big minutes and sit 144th and 153rd of 233 centers, and Dylan Larkin has appeared in only 10 of 18 games.

The recent slide is real in the standings: 1-4-0 over the last five, 2.4 goals scored and 3.6 allowed a game. The loss of points this season is a story about outcomes rather than about the underlying play falling apart. The bet here is that the shooting percentage climbs toward normal and the record follows, provided the crease tilts toward whichever goalie is stopping pucks.

strengths.title: Controlling play at 5-on-5
strengths.body: Detroit owns a .531 share of 5-on-5 expected goals and a .52 share of shot attempts, both top ten. That is a sharp break from five straight seasons below .49. The shot gap backs it up in all situations, 28.8 for against 23.3 against. Because it shows up in both the attempts and the chance-quality measures, it is the most durable thing on this sheet.

strengths.title: Suppressing shots, limiting blueline damage
strengths.body: The team allows 3.7 fewer shots a game than the league average. Opposing defensemen score below expectation against it (rank 8). The 10th-ranked defense by goals against is a product of volume control, not goalie heroics. It should hold as long as the structure does.

strengths.title: A wing trio carrying the scoring
strengths.body: Raymond, DeBrincat and Arvidsson rank 16th, 14th and 13th on their tabs and all drive play above .54 xGF %. DeBrincat's 66 shots for 7 goals is the clearest case of a shooter due for more. Brandsegg-Nygård (17th among right wings, +9) and Finnie add a second wave of positive possession.

concerns.title: Last in the league at finishing
concerns.body: A .091 shooting percentage, 32nd of 32, is the main reason a top-ten chance team scores like a bottom-six one. Some of it is the roster: the depth centers Copp and Rasmussen have three goals between them on heavy minutes. But a gap this far below the league's .116 is mostly noise and should rise. How fast it rises decides whether Detroit climbs back in time.

concerns.title: Gibson's starts are costing games
concerns.body: Gibson has made most of the starts and posted a .860 save % and -5.9 GSAx. Tarasov sits at .919 and +6.5 in fewer appearances. Small samples both, but the split is stark enough that leaning on Gibson is a choice with a measurable price. The D+ goaltending grade reflects it.

concerns.title: A penalty kill bleeding goals
concerns.body: At 69%, the PK ranks 28th, eight points under the league average. It echoes the 2024-25 kill at .701. This looks less like pure bad luck and more like a recurring structural weakness. With 5-on-5 play this good, special teams are where the standings points are leaking.

trend.note: A 6-8 October gave way to a 1-3 start to November. The last five games went 1-4-0 at 2.4 goals scored and 3.6 allowed a game, the worst stretch of the season, ending in a 0-4 loss at Colorado.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, ending against one of the league's best
weekAhead.body:
All three games are away, against teams Detroit has already seen. It lost 5-4 at home to St. Louis, won 5-3 in Florida and lost 4-2 in Tampa. St. Louis is the softest matchup on paper. It allows 28.5 shots a game (25th), the kind of leaky shot suppression Detroit's volume game should exploit. The catch is a B+ goaltending group with a .899 save % and an 84.4% PK, a bad combination for a team that can't finish.

Florida mirrors Detroit: strong possession (.55 CF %, 4th), few shots allowed, a 85.7% PK (5th) and a .886 save %. Expect a tight, low-event game. Tampa Bay, 4th on the site, is the class of the week: .56 xGF %, 6th in offense, A and A+ skater grades. Two points out of three games would be acceptable; four would be a statement.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit centers against soft middles
keyMatchups.body: St. Louis gives centers 0.47 points a game above their expectation (26th). Florida gives up 0.36 above (22nd). Finnie has been Detroit's productive center, while Copp and Rasmussen have produced little despite big minutes. If Larkin is in the lineup, this is the week the middle of the ice should produce.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's weak special teams
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's 69% kill is its biggest leak, but Tampa's power play converts only 19.4% (23rd). Its own PK is 72.9% (24th). Against the toughest opponent of the week, special teams are the one phase where Detroit isn't outclassed.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's defensemen get loose
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's defense lets opposing defensemen score 0.27 points a game over expectation (28th). Seider (10 assists, 25.9 minutes) and Faulk (30th on the defense tab) are positioned to take advantage from the point.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in goal. Two or more Tarasov starts on this road trip would signal Detroit is addressing its biggest fixable problem.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 77 points undersells this team. A top-ten xGF % with the league's worst shooting percentage is the classic profile of a club whose results lag its play. Over 64 remaining games Detroit's shooting should drift toward the league norm, which alone would lift it from 27th in offense toward the middle. The shot suppression is real and should keep goals against in the top half. A Tarasov-leaning crease would add more.

What won't fix itself is the penalty kill, which has been poor before. A division with Boston, Montreal and Tampa all well ahead also caps the upside. The realistic target is a range of roughly 80 to 90 points: better than the pace, but only a bubble contender in a crowded Atlantic. It does not take a playoff berth for granted after an 18-game hole.
swingFactors: Shooting % recovering toward the league norm
Penalty kill climbing out of the bottom five

confidence.note: 18 games; possession numbers are stable, finishing and goalie splits are small samples.
